why.Crest trail north from Stevens Pass: When the gravel Smith Brook road is still under snow or closed, since this start needs no spur road, at the price of a few more miles.

review.notes: Checked online: the lake is reached either by the Smithbrook Trail on a Forest Service road (high clearance advised) or by the Pacific Crest Trail from Stevens Pass; snow lingers into early summer. Reason matches. No closure notice found.

why.Heliotrope Ridge and the Thunder Glacier: When the Middle Fork Nooksack road is closed or washed out; the Heliotrope road is usually open, but expect far more roped glacier travel.

review.notes: Checked online: trip reports confirm the Middle Fork Nooksack road and Rankin Creek line is the direct approach, with a ski or glacier approach over the Thunder Glacier from Heliotrope as the alternative. The road-closed trigger is from stored notes; no current status found.

why.Cold Springs and the Round the Mountain: When the Bird Creek Meadows side is closed, as it has been in some years, or you are camped on the south side; a longer walk east across the lava flows to reach the same moraine.

review.notes: Checked online: parties have used the Cold Springs line when the Bird Creek trailhead was closed (2008, 2016, 2017, 2018), and the Bird Creek climbers' trail is steeper but shorter and needs a tribal permit. Current-year status not found.

why.Start and finish at Cold Springs: For a loop from the south-side trailhead, or when you would rather not drive the gravel roads to Killen Creek; it starts with the steep South Climb trail.

review.notes: Checked online: both starts are used, with Killen Creek the usual preference for the full loop and Cold Springs also listed as a start. The earlier 'slightly shorter' claim was not backed by a source and was dropped.

why.Artist Point and Ptarmigan Ridge to the: When coming at the ridge from the Artist Point side, for example linking it with other Park Glacier objectives; far longer than Heliotrope, and the road there is closed by snow much of the year.

review.notes: Checked online: the Ptarmigan Ridge trail from Artist Point is long, snow covered into July, and the road to Artist Point closes for the season (a late-October 2026 notice says the highway to Artist Point has closed). No page described the Cockscomb itself, so the linking reason rests on stored notes.
fromStoredNotes: Artist Point and Ptarmigan Ridge to the Park Glacier

review.notes: Skipped: the only non-primary way, the south gully, is the climb itself rather than a separate way in, and its stored notes give no honest reason to choose it over the Slate Pass start. Nothing written.

problems: Non-primary way 'The south gully below the Carru-Lago col' reads as the climb itself; its notes instead describe two approaches (Slate Pass vs the longer Monument Creek trail), neither matching the way name.

why.Baker River Trail and the Pioneer Ridge: For strong cross-country parties who want the southwest flank from the Baker River trailhead instead of the Chilliwack ford; rarely done, so check the Baker Lake road first.

review.notes: Partly checked: the Hannegan Pass line does need a Chilliwack River wade, and the Baker River approach is described as almost never used. No page describes a Crowder climb from the Pioneer Ridge side, so that part rests on stored notes. Baker Lake Road closure: a Forest Service alert page (FSR 11 closed at Shannon Creek Bridge from about mid-July) was found in search snippets but showed no year and the page now returns not found, so the 2026 status is unconfirmed.
fromStoredNotes: Baker River Trail and the Pioneer Ridge high route

review.notes: Skipped: the non-primary way is the glacier and summit leg after Glacier Meadows, and its notes call it the standard line, so no honest alternative-approach reason can be written.

problems: Non-primary way 'Glacier Meadows to the summit block via Snow Dome and Crystal Pass' is a continuation of the primary (Hoh River Trail to Glacier Meadows), not an alternative, and its notes say the Park points climbers to it as the standard.

why.From the Sulphide Glacier, across the Cr: When you want the ridge as a short outing from the standard Sulphide Glacier route, skipping the North Face; cross the Crystal Glacier to the ridge foot.

review.notes: Checked online: rangers have climbed the ridge after crossing the Crystal Glacier from the Sulphide Glacier, finding it straightforward with a few small crevasses; the North Face route also crosses both glaciers. Reason matches.

why.Esmeralda, Ingalls Lake and Stuart Pass: When approaching from the south side, over Ingalls and Stuart Passes to Goat Pass, with a high bivy and a short drop onto the glacier; the northern Mountaineer Creek route is longer.

review.notes: Checked online: the Goat Pass line from Ingalls Lake is a described approach to the glacier, while the Mountaineer Creek approach from the north is longer. Reworded to drop an unsupported claim about the Stuart Lake road end.

why.Kautz Creek Trail to Indian Henry's: A shorter but steeper way to Indian Henry's than Longmire; the creek crossing is often damaged, and the trail has been reported closed there, so ask about it first.

review.notes: Checked online: Kautz Creek is a bit shorter and steeper than the Longmire trail. A trail-page notice dated 1.2.26 reports the trail closed at the Kautz Creek crossing until further notice; current status not confirmed.

why.Snowy Creek trail from Smith Brook road: For a shorter, gentler and more scenic climb than the steep highway trail; it is north facing, so snow lingers, and the road has had storm damage, so check it is open.

review.notes: Checked online: the trail page states Snowy Creek Road (FR 6705) is closed until further notice due to storm damage, with a notice date written 6.3.26 (day and month order unclear); no reopening notice found. It also confirms the Snowy Creek line is shorter, less steep and holds snow longer, while the highway line is drier and favoured early season.

why.Lake Chelan: Lucerne and Emerald Park to: When you are already on the Lake Chelan side with a boat ride to Lucerne; a long remote approach over Milham Pass instead of the North Fork Entiat road.

review.notes: Checked online: the Entiat approach is the most direct, and the Emerald Park approach starts by boat at Lucerne and crosses Milham Pass. Reason matches.

why.Silver Star Creek from the north: In spring on continuous snow, as a ski or snowshoe approach that avoids the steep Burgundy Col slope; longer, and once the valley melts out it turns brushy and swampy.

review.notes: Checked online: guides call the Silver Star Creek line a good spring ski or snowshoe trip and an alternative to the shorter but much steeper Burgundy Col approach. Reworded to say longer and to avoid the steep slope.

why.Lake Ann and the Fisher Chimneys to the: When you want to camp at Lake Ann or above the chimneys on a multi-day trip and accept scrambling with rockfall risk; longer and more technical than Shannon Ridge.

review.notes: Checked online: the chimneys route is described as more challenging than the Sulphide approach, with rockfall a concern in the chimneys, and a camp at Lake Ann. No page covered the southeast ridge finish itself.

why.Downey Creek and the Chickamin Glacier: When starting from the Suiattle River road without the Stehekin boat and shuttle; a long brushy approach, then roped travel over the Chickamin Glacier to the Gunsight peaks.

review.notes: Checked online: the Agnes Creek line from Stehekin is called possibly the best access but needs the ferry and shuttle, while the Downey and Bachelor Creek line is a long brush bash that crosses the Chickamin Glacier. Reworded from the earlier 'bushwhack' framing, which had the two reversed.

why.From the valley on the east, reaching th: When coming up from the Stehekin valley by boat instead of crossing the pass; the climb to the lake is off trail, steep and brushy, and the way is not marked.

review.notes: Checked online: the lake is reached by a steep off-trail climb from the upper Stehekin River trail, mostly bushwhacking, which matches the stored caution. Floatplane access was not found, so the wording says boat only. Published accounts remain thin.

problems: The east-valley way's drainage and distance are described inconsistently, so its detail is unreliable.
